title: The Bog Bodies
text: Bodies in the peat, perfectly kept, faces calm, skin brown and smooth as tanned leather. Some still wear gold at their throats and rings on their fingers. The marsh folk say they were offerings, given to the bog so it would give something back.

options.label: Take the gold from their throats.

outcomes.text: Old gold, cold and heavy, and the faces do not change.
The bodies sit up, peat sliding off their faces, and reach for what was theirs.

options.label: The wisest studies the marks on them.

outcomes.text: Marks of the old marsh gods, cut into the skin, and the god's names, and what each was given for.
The peat closes over their calm faces. The marsh seems grateful, and opens a dry path ahead.
